description:
Coreutils edge cases: arithmetic, format directives, the locale, huge widths and non-regular inputs.

Every case name starts with "coreutils: ".

cases.name: coreutils: wc single file no padding
cases.script:
printf 'a
b
c
' > f; wc -l f; wc -l f | cut -d' ' -f1

cases.name: coreutils: wc single file width from its own counts, not byte size
cases.script: for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do printf '%01000d\n' 0; done > f; wc -l f; wc -l f | cut -d' ' -f1

cases.name: coreutils: wc redirected stdin sizes from its own counts
cases.script: for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do printf '%01000d\n' 0; done > f; wc < f; wc -l < f; wc -lc < f

cases.name: coreutils: wc true pipe still widens to 7
cases.script: for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do printf '%01000d\n' 0; done | wc; for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do printf '%01000d\n' 0; done | wc -l

cases.name: coreutils: wc multi-file widens by summed byte size
cases.script:
printf 'a
b
c
' > f; printf 'd
e
' > g; wc -l f g

cases.name: coreutils: wc mixed file and stdin widens like GNU
cases.script:
printf 'a
b
c
' > f; printf 'x
' | wc -l - f

cases.name: coreutils: wc files0-from zero-length entry does not widen the other rows
cases.script: cd /tmp; echo hi > a.txt; printf 'a.txt\0\0' > list0; wc --files0-from=list0; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: seq with an infinite end streams until head stops it
cases.script: seq 1 inf | head -n 2; echo s=$?; seq 5 inf | head -n 2

cases.name: coreutils: seq with a huge end streams
cases.script: seq 1 1e20 | head -n 2

cases.name: coreutils: seq large integer increment does not overshoot
coreutils: seq format with no directive is an error
cases.script: seq -f x 1 2; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: seq rejects nan
cases.script: seq nan 1 3; echo s=$?; seq 1 nan 3; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: seq long-form separator and format take a space-separated argument
cases.script: seq --separator , 1 3; seq --format %g 1 3

cases.name: coreutils: find -mtime excludes a file well under N days old
cases.script: cd /tmp && touch -d '1 hour ago' fresh; find . -maxdepth 1 -name fresh -mtime -2; find . -maxdepth 1 -name fresh -mtime 2; find . -maxdepth 1 -name fresh -mtime +1

cases.name: coreutils: find -mtime matches a file well over N days old
cases.script: cd /tmp && touch -d '3 days ago' old; find . -maxdepth 1 -name old -mtime -2; find . -maxdepth 1 -name old -mtime 2; find . -maxdepth 1 -name old -mtime +1

cases.name: coreutils: which finds this crate's own commands and Brush builtins that are real programs
cases.script: which sed; echo s=$?; which cat ls; echo s=$?; which echo; echo s=$?; which cd; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: which with no operands is an error
cases.script: which; echo s=$?

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: xargs does not run shell builtins
cases.script: echo /tmp | xargs cd; echo "s=$? pwd=$(pwd)"; echo X=1 | xargs export; echo "s=$? X=${X-unset}"

cases.name: coreutils: find -exec does not run shell builtins
cases.script: cd /tmp && find /tmp -maxdepth 0 -exec cd {} \; ; echo "find s=$? pwd=$(pwd)"

cases.name: coreutils: xargs and find -exec still run this crate's own commands
cases.script: echo /tmp | xargs ls -d; cd /tmp && find /tmp -maxdepth 0 -exec echo {} \;

cases.name: coreutils: xargs and find -exec still run echo (a real GNU program, not a shell builtin)
cases.script: printf 'a b\nc\n' | xargs echo; echo s=$?; cd /tmp && find /tmp -maxdepth 0 -exec echo hi {} \;

cases.name: coreutils: cp refuses a symlink of the same file instead of emptying it
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf important-data > f; ln -s f l; cp f l; echo s=$?; cat f

cases.name: coreutils: cp refuses two symlinks to the same file
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf data > t; ln -s t a; ln -s t b; cp a b; echo s=$?; cat t

cases.name: coreutils: cp still copies a genuinely different file onto a symlink
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf one > a; printf two > b; ln -s b l; cp a l; echo s=$?; cat l

cases.name: coreutils: base64 -D is not a GNU option
cases.script: printf aGk= | base64 -D; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: base64 -d rejects a stray CR
cases.script: printf 'aGVsbG8K\r\n' | base64 -d; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: tr rejects an equivalence class in string2 when translating
cases.script: printf abc | tr abc '[=x=]'; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: truncate rejects a hex size
cases.script: cd /tmp; truncate -s 0x10 f 2>&1; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: factor rejects a padded operand
cases.script: factor ' 15 '; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: stat rejects an unknown short option
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf abc > f; stat -c %n -@ f; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: stat rejects an unknown long option
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf abc > f; stat --bogus f; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: stat --printf has no trailing newline of its own
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf 12345 > f; stat --printf '%s\n' f; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: stat %F says regular empty file for a zero-byte file
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch e; printf abc > f; stat -c %F e; stat -c %F f

cases.name: coreutils: stat %N quotes the name and shows a symlink's target
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf abc > f; ln -s f l; stat -c %N f; stat -c %N l

cases.name: coreutils: stat %a/%A/%U/%G/%u/%g report this sandbox's fixed defaults
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf abc > f; stat -c '%a|%A|%U:%G|%u:%g' f; mkdir d; stat -c '%a|%A' d

cases.name: coreutils: cut -c splits on characters, not UTF-8 bytes
cases.script: printf 'caf\303\251 ok\n' | cut -c1-4

cases.name: coreutils: expr length/substr count characters
cases.script: expr length héllo; expr substr héllo 1 3

cases.name: coreutils: fold -b still splits on bytes even in a UTF-8 locale
cases.script: printf 'aaaaaaaaaaaaa\n' | fold -b -w5

cases.name: coreutils: md5sum -c prints a non-ASCII name as characters
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf hi > f; md5sum f > sums; touch é; md5sum é >> sums 2>/dev/null; md5sum -c sums 2>&1 | tail -1

cases.name: coreutils: stat -f is refused
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf abc > f; stat -f f; echo s=$?

stderr.text: stat: -f is unsupported in bash-tool: no real filesystem statistics in the sandbox

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: stat -t is refused
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf abc > f; stat -t f; echo s=$?

stderr.text: stat: -t is unsupported in bash-tool: no real device/inode data in the sandbox

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: sort keeps each file's unterminated last line separate
cases.script: printf b > /tmp/sx; printf a > /tmp/sy; sort /tmp/sx /tmp/sy

cases.name: coreutils: readlink -f of an empty path fails
cases.script: readlink -f ''; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: mv into a missing directory names both paths
cases.script: printf x > /tmp/mvsrc; mv /tmp/mvsrc /tmp/nosuchdir/mvdst; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: ln of a missing source says failed to access
cases.script: ln /tmp/nosuch-src /tmp/lndst; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: find -printf refuses an oversized field width
cases.script: touch /tmp/fpw; find /tmp/fpw -printf '%999999999999p\n'; echo s=$?

stderr.text: find: -printf with a field width this large is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: numfmt refuses an oversized --padding
cases.script: numfmt --padding=99999999 5 | wc -c; echo s=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

stderr.text: numfmt: --padding above 16777216 is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: cmp -l pads the offset column to the compared length
cases.script:
printf 'abcdef
line2
' >/tmp/cl1; printf 'abXdef
line2
' >/tmp/cl2; cmp -l /tmp/cl1 /tmp/cl2

cases.name: coreutils: cmp -b reports GNU's byte/char wording
cases.script: printf '\007x' >/tmp/cb1; printf '\001y' >/tmp/cb2; cmp -b /tmp/cb1 /tmp/cb2

cases.name: coreutils: cmp -lb names every control and high-bit byte
coreutils: od -t f4 uses scientific notation for a large float
cases.script: printf 'o, W' | od -An -t f4

cases.name: coreutils: od -t f8 uses scientific notation for a large float
coreutils: nl -v accepts a negative starting number
cases.script: nl -v -2 /dev/null; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: nl -s pads an unnumbered line to the real separator width
cases.script:
printf 'a

b
' | nl -s ': ' | od -c | head -n 3

cases.name: coreutils: numfmt normalizes a tab separator to a space, not verbatim
cases.script: printf '2048\ta\n' | numfmt --to iec --format '%-5f'

cases.name: coreutils: numfmt preserves a run of spaces beyond the first
cases.script: printf '2048   a   b\n' | numfmt --to iec

cases.name: coreutils: join drops a phantom trailing field from trailing whitespace
cases.script: printf '1 a  \n' >/tmp/jtw1; printf '1 b\n' >/tmp/jtw2; join /tmp/jtw1 /tmp/jtw2

cases.name: coreutils: sort -t accepts a non-UTF-8 byte separator
cases.script: x=$'\xff'; printf 'a1\nb2\n' | sort -t "$x" -k2; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: expr accepts a non-UTF-8 byte in its argument
cases.script: x=$'\xff'; expr "a$x" : 'a.'; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: numfmt --suffix accepts a non-UTF-8 byte
cases.script: x=$'\xff'; numfmt --suffix="$x" 5; echo s=$?

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: rmdir accepts a trailing slash
cases.script: mkdir -p /tmp/rmdts; rmdir /tmp/rmdts/; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: fmt fills to GNU's actual goal width, not one word short
cases.script: seq 60 | paste -s -d ' ' | fmt -w 75

cases.name: coreutils: fmt's sentence spacing doesn't overflow the requested width
cases.script: printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It barked.  Then it ran away quickly. The end.\n' | fmt -w 40

cases.name: coreutils: dd if/of/skip/count with status=none matches byte-for-byte
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf '0123456789' > din; dd if=din of=dout bs=1 skip=2 count=3 status=none; cat dout; echo; rm -f din dout

cases.name: coreutils: dd conv=notrunc seek writes into the middle of an existing file
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf 'AAAAAAAAAA' > dout2; printf 'XX' | dd of=dout2 bs=1 seek=3 conv=notrunc status=none; cat dout2; echo; rm -f dout2

cases.name: coreutils: du -a lists every path in the tree, not just directories
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p dutree/sub; printf a > dutree/f1; printf bb > dutree/sub/f2; du -a dutree | cut -f2 | sort; rm -rf dutree

cases.name: coreutils: du -c prints a grand total line after the named operands
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p da db; printf a > da/f; printf bb > db/f; du -c -s da db | cut -f2; rm -rf da db

cases.name: coreutils: chmod refuses canonically instead of pretending to succeed
cases.script: cd /tmp; touch c; chmod 644 c; echo s=$?; rm -f c

stderr.text: chmod: changing file modes is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: nproc reports this sandbox's one logical core
cases.script: nproc; echo s=$?

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: hostname answers from GOLEM_AGENT_ID
cases.script: hostname; echo s=$?

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: uname -a reports this sandbox's fixed, synthetic fields
cases.script: uname -a; echo s=$?

stdout.text:
Linux conformance-agent 6.1.0 #1 SMP wasm32 GNU/Linux
s=0

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: cp -p copies from a /dev/fd/N pipe instead of refusing it
cases.script: exec 3< <(printf 'hello\n'); cp -p /dev/fd/3 /tmp/cpfd.$$; cat /tmp/cpfd.$$; echo s=$?; rm -f /tmp/cpfd.$$

cases.name: coreutils: cp -a and cp -rp keep a directory's and a symlink's times
cases.script: mkdir -p /tmp/s/sub; ln -s gone /tmp/s/l; touch -d '2001-02-03 04:05:06' /tmp/s/sub/ /tmp/s; touch -h -d '2002-03-04 05:06:07' /tmp/s/l; cd /tmp; cp -a s a; echo st=$?; cp -rp s p; echo st=$?; stat -c '%n %Y' a a/sub a/l p p/sub p/l

cases.name: coreutils: file recognizes a JSON object and array
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf '{"a":1}' > j1.json; file j1.json; printf '[1,2,3]' > j2.json; file j2.json; rm -f j1.json j2.json

cases.name: coreutils: file recognizes JSON with leading whitespace and nesting
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf '  \n  {"a":{"b":2}}\n' > j3.json; file j3.json; rm -f j3.json

cases.name: coreutils: file does not recognize invalid JSON
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf '{not json' > j4.json; file j4.json; rm -f j4.json

cases.name: coreutils: file does not recognize a bare JSON scalar
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf '42' > jn.json; file jn.json; printf 'true' > jt.json; file jt.json; rm -f jn.json jt.json

cases.name: coreutils: file does not recognize JSON with trailing garbage
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf '{"a":1} extra' > jx.json; file jx.json; rm -f jx.json

cases.name: coreutils: file's --mime-type and -i for JSON
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf '{"a":1}\n' > j5.json; file --mime-type j5.json; file -i j5.json; rm -f j5.json

cases.name: coreutils: file recognizes a large JSON array
cases.script: cd /tmp; { printf '['; seq 1 100000 | tr '\n' ','; printf '0]'; } > jbig.json; file jbig.json; rm -f jbig.json

cases.name: coreutils: install copies a single file
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf hello > isrc; install isrc idest; cat idest; echo s=$?; rm -f isrc idest

cases.name: coreutils: install with no operands is an error
cases.script: install; echo s=$?

cases.name: coreutils: install refuses a directory source
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p idsrc; install idsrc iddst; echo s=$?; rm -rf idsrc iddst

cases.name: coreutils: install -d creates a directory tree
cases.script: cd /tmp; install -d itree/sub; ls itree; echo s=$?; rm -rf itree

cases.name: coreutils: install -D creates the destination's parents and copies
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf hi > idsrc2; install -D idsrc2 ia/ib/idest2; cat ia/ib/idest2; echo s=$?; rm -rf idsrc2 ia

cases.name: coreutils: install -t copies several sources into a target directory
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p itdir; printf a > ita; printf b > itb; install -t itdir ita itb; ls itdir; echo s=$?; rm -rf itdir ita itb

cases.name: coreutils: install -v reports what it did
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf x > ivsrc; install -v ivsrc ivdest; echo s=$?; rm -f ivsrc ivdest; install -v -d ivdir; echo s=$?; rm -rf ivdir

cases.name: coreutils: install -b backs up an existing destination
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf old > ibdest; printf new > ibsrc; install -b ibsrc ibdest; cat ibdest; cat ibdest~; echo s=$?; rm -f ibsrc ibdest ibdest~

cases.name: coreutils: install -m/-o/-g are accepted and ignored
cases.script: cd /tmp; printf x > imsrc; install -m 755 -o nobody -g nogroup imsrc imdest; cat imdest; echo s=$?; rm -f imsrc imdest

expected.reason: documented cosmetic gap; see the case's own comment

cases.name: coreutils: ls -C wraps to one column when nothing wider fits
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p lsw; cd lsw; touch aaa bb ccccccc d ee fffffffffff; ls -C -w 20

cases.name: coreutils: ls -C columns and their tab-stop fill at a middling width
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p lsw2; cd lsw2; touch aaa bb ccccccc d ee fffffffffff g hhhhh; ls -C -w 40

cases.name: coreutils: ls -x fills left-to-right instead of top-to-bottom
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p lsw3; cd lsw3; touch aaa bb ccccccc d ee fffffffffff g hhhhh; ls -x -w 40

cases.name: coreutils: ls -C at a width wide enough for one line uses plain spaces, not tabs
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p lsw4; cd lsw4; touch aaa bb ccccccc d ee fffffffffff g hhhhh; ls -C -w 80
